Prevention: Prevent all potatoes from growing that have not been planted.
Those growing from last years crop and especially potato dumps need to be controlled over a wide area.
Remove navo plants and previous crop residue/weeds from the field and burn.
Use planting material from reliable sources eg. registered agro-dealers, government farm.
Select healthy seeds for planting (a good seed size is 25-40 gm).
Adjust planting date according to the weather to prevent appropriate weather condition for disease development.
Potash/ ropani, splitting it 2.5kg urea at field preparation and 4.5kg during earthing- up stage.
Cut off the tops of the plants at maturity prior to harvest.
This will prevent tops becoming infected and spreading symptoms down to the tubers.
Monitoring: Wet, foggy and frosty conditions are ideal for infection and spread.
In these conditions, monitor your crop everyday.
Look for downy growth & watery soaked lesions on the underside of leaves and brown lesions on the upper side.
If symptoms exist go for immediate intervention.
If it is not wet, foggy or frosty check your crop once a week.
Direct Control: Once symptoms are seen, there is nothing that can be done to stop the disease without chemicals.
Phytophthora is not a true fungus and many fungicides typcially used on crops will have no effect on this disease.
Mix in stickers to improve the persistence of the pesticides.
Restrictions: These pesticides are in order of priority.
Ensure you do not repeatedly use the same chemical repeatedly in isolation.
Use protective equipment when filling the sprayer and spraying.
Gloves, boots, overalls and eye protection should be put on.
